clue.text: Hot matter's modified by temperature controller

indicators.note: modified means changed in form, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the S counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Something hot alters its state under the influence of temperature, like a physics lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges HOTMATTERS; here the S of matter's is needed as a letter, the apostrophe simply dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat is the device that switches heating or cooling on and off to hold a set temperature.

clue.text: Mite given indication of approval

explanation.surface: A tiny creature receives a nod of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a small blood-sucking arachnid related to mites, and also the check mark a teacher puts beside a right answer.

clue.text: Some man evil neigbour upset making fire

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the run of letters is read from bottom to top
some of the words means only part of their letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A wicked neighbour, angered, is getting heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks NEVILNE from maN EVIL NEigbour and 'upset' turns it round. The clue's misspelt 'neigbour' does not affect the letters used.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up, in the sense of rousing them, is to liven them up or animate them.

clue.text: What professors of composition get, being game?

explanation.surface: A wry question about what music academics are given, answered by a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: A professor holds a chair, so professors of music hold musical chairs; the same words name the party game where players scramble for seats when the music stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairs are professorships, and those in music are musical ones; it is also the children's party game of circling seats until the music stops.

clue.text: Having several parts that make for good luck?

definitions.text: Having several parts that make for good luck?

parts.words: Having several parts that make for good luck?
parts.note: seven is traditionally the lucky number, so something with that many parts is the fortunate kind of multiple

explanation.surface: A question about some object whose components bring good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Septuple means sevenfold, consisting of seven parts, and seven is the proverbial lucky number.

clue.text: Room bill must keep dry on island

indicators.note: must keep means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: A room's bill has to account for a dry spell on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal, a dry drinker; AC is an account or bill. In a down clue 'on' sets the island below the rest, and 'must keep' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the space or room just under the roof of a house.

clue.text: Commotion in street — I run

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone describes running down the road during a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a fuss or excited disturbance, as in 'caused quite a stir'.

clue.text: The heartless girl's time in a flat?

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted young woman spends her time in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the central H of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the period during which someone rents and occupies a property such as a flat.

clue.text: American bird — one doing the marathon?

explanation.surface: A US bird species, and a jogger tackling a long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: A marathon is run on roads, so its entrant is literally a runner of the road: the pun on the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a fast ground-dwelling cuckoo of the southwestern US, and someone running on streets is literally running the road.

clue.text: Guns for little boys?

explanation.surface: A question about toy firearms made for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt is a famous firearms maker, and a colt is a young male horse, here stretched to young boys or juniors.
explanation.definitionFit: Colts are revolvers from the Colt company, and colts are young male horses, also used of inexperienced youngsters or junior players.

clue.text: The old man with a goat in wild plateau region

parts.note: PA is a familiar word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the three words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Dad and a goat run loose in some untamed upland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges GOATIN into TAGONI; the clue's 'a' is set beside it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the southern part of South America, much of it a vast arid plateau.

clue.text: Gets destroyed? Message from Indians does!

explanation.surface: Something is ruined, and Native Americans' messages rise skywards as signals.
explanation.walkthrough: The old Western image of smoke signals: a message sent that way rises in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To be burnt away or come to nothing is the idiom; a smoke signal literally rises in the vapour of a fire.

clue.text: Sucker employed for dirty work

parts.note: sucker sounds like a dupe exploited by villains, but here it is a household appliance that sucks up dust

explanation.surface: A gullible stooge is hired for an underhand job.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic appliance that draws in dust and dirt by suction, used for cleaning floors.

clue.text: Groups of hopefuls making provisions for minor shopping sprees?

definitions.text: making provisions for minor shopping sprees

explanation.surface: Candidates' lists, and brief notes for small trips to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: brief lists of things to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the final selection of candidates for a job or prize; literally, brief lists drawn up for small shopping trips.

clue.text: House number needed to get to girl in island port

parts.note: Lulu is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone needs a house number to find a young woman in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital and main harbour of Hawaii, on the island of Oahu.

clue.text: Writer with no important point? The reverse!

indicators.note: the reverse means the pieces just given are turned back to front

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
the nub is the crux or central point of a matter

explanation.surface: A writer who never makes a significant point, or quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse!' looks like a comment on the surface, but it turns NAYNUB end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan was the 17th-century English author of The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: Something put in garden that may later bring you to tears?

definitions.text: Something put in garden that may later bring you to tears?

parts.words: Something put in garden that may later bring you to tears?
parts.note: the planting that grows into a bulb which, once chopped in the kitchen, makes the eyes water

explanation.surface: A gardener's planting with a melancholy future.
explanation.definitionFit: A small immature bulb planted to grow a full-sized one; that vegetable famously stings the eyes when cut.

clue.text: Hooligans mentioned 'frills'

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for frills is said aloud to give a word sounding the same

parts.note: ruffs are pleated frilled collars

explanation.surface: Rowdy youths were said to be wearing frilly collars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' signals a homophone: RUFFS, frilled collars, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughs is a dated word for violent, rowdy men, thugs.

clue.text: Ignorant woman? Women primarily are!

parts.note: Una is a woman's name

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A jibe that a woman is clueless, answered with the retort that all women are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the W of Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware means lacking knowledge of something, oblivious.

clue.text: O to do this!

parts.note: read as a wish, but the letter O is shaped like a ring and so does this to its centre

explanation.surface: A poetic exclamation of longing, 'O to do this!'
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a poet's 'O to be in England'; the O is in fact the round letter, which surrounds a space.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle is to form a ring around, which is exactly what the shape of a round letter does.

clue.text: Fellow at lunchtime gets bread

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow
one o'clock is lunchtime, and I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man takes a loaf at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is one o'clock, giving I, Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Town that could be pleasing to man

indicators.note: could be means the following letters may be turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A place that might delight a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges PLEASINGTOMAN. LEAMINGTON SPA is a Warwickshire spa town in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Leamington Spa is a spa town in Warwickshire, England.

clue.text: Lively line from Russian author

parts.note: go-go means lively and energetic

explanation.surface: A spirited line taken from a Russian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the 19th-century writer of Dead Souls and The Government Inspector.

clue.text: Very little drink? There could be a river here!

definitions.text: There could be a river here!

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, a little of the word
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A sip of beer, and a note on where a stream might run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' reads as a tiny amount; it is V, the abbreviation of very.
explanation.definitionFit: A vale is a valley, the low ground where a stream or river typically flows.

clue.text: Twelve groups making nightly appearances

parts.note: sounds like a troupe of performers on stage each night, but means the dozen zodiac constellations visible in the night sky

explanation.surface: A dozen acts performing every evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve zodiac divisions, each named after a constellation of stars seen at night.

clue.text: Sailor starts to appear keen approaching port

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A sailor seems eager as he nears the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes A, K, A from appear, keen, approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese seaport city on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Horse losing time in race

indicators.note: losing means the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: A horse falls behind during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is not a contest here but lineage; 'losing' drops T from STEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed in the biblical sense means offspring or descendants, a family line or race.

clue.text: Everybody must face the enemy without any let-up

parts.note: all means everybody
time is the enemy in the saying 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: Everyone has to confront the foe without rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is the phrase behind enemy = TIME; 'must face' just places ALL first.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantly, continuously, at every moment without pause.
